headline: Paris fell 1-0 behind at 18 minutes, then scored five unanswered; right-back Achraf Hakimi scored three and set up two.

team_story.label: Shots on target
team_story.why_it_matters: Shot volume was level (14 v 15) but PSG put twice as many on target

team_story.label: Through balls
team_story.why_it_matters: PSG kept splitting the Le Havre back three

team_story.label: Passes
team_story.why_it_matters: PSG 777 passes at 92% accuracy, Le Havre 303 at 80%

tactical_change.trigger: Falling 1-0 to a Le Havre counter-attack (3-4-2-1, pressing high)
tactical_change.effect: No shape change in the sources. PSG scored 5 times between the 26th and 69th minute; their first two changes came at 63' and 71' once they led 4-1.

best_player.name: Achraf Hakimi
best_player.why: First career hat-trick from right-back plus two assists: a hand in all five PSG goals.
best_player.source: https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/50330654/psg-achraf-hakimi-hat-trick-luis-enrique-wins-record-le-havre ('playing a role in all five goals', 'first career hat trick and provided two assists'); https://www.psg.fr/en/content/achraf-hakimi-leads-paris-to-another-win-in-le-havre-match-report-le-havre-ac-paris-saint-germain-ligue-1-2026-2027

caveats: No player ratings on the web path; best is Scout's pick. No worst player named (no ratings or error data).
ESPN shot-map rows (players, minutes and Goal labels) do not match the official goal timeline, so the shot map is not used for any claim.
ESPN story text puts Hakimi's treble goal in the 69th minute right after describing Mayulu's goal; PSG.fr and the ESPN scoreboard give Mayulu 62' and Hakimi 69'. The reel uses the scoreboard minutes.
No possession or xG on the cached pages, so neither is used.
